passage:
On the train to the city, Lily always wanted the window seat. She liked watching mountains, rivers, and houses pass by.
One day, an old woman got on the train and stood beside Lily's seat. There were no other seats left. Lily wanted to keep looking out the window, but she also saw the woman holding a heavy bag.
After a moment, Lily stood up and offered the seat. The woman thanked her and sat down.
Lily stood near the door. At first, she felt disappointed. Then she noticed something new. From there, she could see people getting on and off, helping each other, and saying goodbye.
She learned that giving up one view can sometimes help you see another.
